text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet minister Maalim Mohamed calls for the extension of the voter registration period by at least two months.
- Some 600 students from the Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology burn down a house and pull down 12 shops over the weekend.
- Mwai Kibaki, chairman of the opposition Democratic Party says the suspension of fund-raising events by the head of state is arbitrary and dictatorial.

- The chairman of the National Democratic Party of Kenya (NDP) issues a three-day ultimatum to Raila Odinga to declare his interest in the national presidency on an NDP ticket and denounce his support for rival Kenneth Matiba.
- Kibaki rejects appeals from ruling party leaders to defect to the ruling party.
- At least 500 primary school pupils in Samburu are yet to report to school following closure last year due to fighting in the area.
- Vice-President George Saitoti says the government is committed to free and fair elections.
- The theory that prominent lawyer Samuel Ndungi was shot by a top cop is dismissed by police headquarters.
- Uganda Airlines plans to start flights to the rebel controlled towns of Goma and Kisangani in East Zaire.

- Envoys from major donor countries have scheduled a meeting in Nairobi this week to review the Kenyan government's response to their demands for minimum reforms before the general election this year.
